messages:
ashley: pagerduty triggered for multiple 5xx alerts in euc2 (AZ D). seeing steady spike across inference endpoints behind NLB. customers reporting errors. https://status.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-103 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-103 (regional euc2 AZ-D ingress 5xx / cross-region routing). incident channel: #incidents. runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/nlb-5xx-spike
vikas_oncall: I'm oncall, taking lead. pinging neteng and support. ashley, can you paste the main alert group?
ashley: alertgroup: nlb-5xx-euc2-azd, ~2000 5xx/min across prod-inference. 90% of errors are connection reset/502 from envoy. stack traces show upstream tcp RSTs.
kevin_neteng: seeing partial probe failures for NLB target group in AZ-D. health checks flapping 50% unhealthy. afaict it's not whole AZ but egress path to edge is dropping packets for some subnets. starting traceroutes to egress gateways.
vikas_oncall: actions: (1) verify target health (2) check envoy metrics / conntrack (3) check Route53 weighted routing and DNS healthchecks (4) if blackhole confirmed, shift weight away from euc2-ez-d.
ashley: running checks, sharing outputs:
```
# aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg/abc
{"TargetsHealth": [{"Target": {"Id": "i-0abcd"}, "State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Connection timed out"}, ...]}
```

maria_support: have ~8 customers impacted (product IDs), some are retrying and seeing degraded latency. Customer A flagged at 10:12 UTC. notifying account teams.
kevin_neteng: traceroute to egress gw in AZ-D shows path drop at provider hop (AS12345) for several IP ranges. filing cloud provider support ticket. possible upstream BGP flapping.
vikas_oncall: Envoy stats (from pod logs) show high downstream `upstream_rq_5xx` and high `downstream_cx_reset` rates. conntrack on nodes is near 95% usage per `ss` output. adding conntrack check: 
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
950000
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
1000000
```

ashley: also seeing bursts of `ENVOY proxy error: recv reset` in logs.
kevin_neteng: two parallel mitigations: (A) ask infra to shift Route53 weighted routing away from euc2->AZ-D to other regions (euc1 primary), (B) drain NLB targets in AZ-D to kick flows off the bad egress path.
vikas_oncall: agree. do (B) first to reduce immediate customer errors, then (A) if we see sustained degradation. kevin, please coordinate weight shift with DNS. maria, escalate impacted customers and enable retries.
dev-deploy-bot: deploy pipeline paused for inference-stable; automatic rollout blocked by ongoing errors.
kevin_neteng: initiating target group drain for AZ-D nodes now. command: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn ... --attributes Key=slow_start.enabled,Value=true` (drain via deregistration- delay set). will update once deregistration completes.
ashley: deregistration started for 6 targets in azd. health in other AZs stable.
maria_support: live update to accounts sent: "We're investigating increased 5xxs in euc2, mitigation in progress, next update in 15m" :mailbox_with_mail:
sarah_product: what's our customer impact tick? Sev2 or Sev1?
vikas_oncall: currently Sev2 (partial regional impact with mitigation under way). escalate to Sev1 only if cross-region traffic or >50% customers impacted.
kevin_neteng: cloud provider responded: "We see packet drops on our transit link affecting traffic from euc2 AZ-D to internet. Mitigation in progress on provider side." they're asking us to shift traffic off that egress.
ashley: Route53 weight change request prepared:
```
# aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc2","Weight":0,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"203.0.113.10"}]}}]}'
```

vikas_oncall: apply weight change to move traffic to euc1 (weight -> 0 for euc2). maria, enable incident banner in status page.
maria_support: banner up. customer comms updated: https://status.redwood/incident/INC-2026-103.
kevin_neteng: making DNS change now. note TTL is 60s.
ashley: after drain + DNS shift we see error rate drop ~70% over 3 minutes. downstream 5xx reduced but still residual.
vikas_oncall: remaining 5xx appear to be from in-cluster conntrack exhaustion and transient retries. infra, can we bump nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes as short-term?
kevin_neteng: submitted infra request to bump on worker pools in euc2-azd to 1.5M, and to recycle pods gracefully. pending approval.
dev-deploy-bot: infra change requested: terraform apply plan-conntrack-bump.
kevin_neteng: provider also reports they rerouted transit for the affected prefixes; this should resolve within propagation.
ashley: timeline so far:
- 10:11 UTC: alerts start
- 10:12 UTC: PagerDuty -> INC-2026-103
- 10:16 UTC: oncall vikas assigned
- 10:20 UTC: target drain AZ-D initiated
- 10:25 UTC: Route53 weight shift to euc1 done (TTL 60)
- 10:28 UTC: 5xx rate drops 70%

maria_support: customers see fewer errors now. reopening tickets and closing them as fixed if no followup within 30m.
sarah_product: any perf regressions from moving traffic to euc1? we saw slightly higher latency (~30ms) on a subset. ok for now.
vikas_oncall: agree to keep traffic steered to euc1 until provider confirms full mitigation. set follow-up tasks: (1) monitor for 1h (2) snapshot conntrack metrics (3) postmortem owner assigned.
kevin_neteng: provider confirms mitigations are stable at 10:40 UTC. we can plan weighted roll-back once we observe stable metrics for 30m.
ashley: metrics stable at 10:55 UTC. preparing controlled roll-back: increment euc2 weight from 0 -> 30 -> 50 over 15m windows.
vikas_oncall: do staged roll-back, watch 5xx and conntrack. do not exceed 50% for first stage.
kevin_neteng: roll-back step 1 applied: euc2 -> 30 at 11:05 UTC. monitoring.
ashley: slight uptick but within baseline. continuing.
maria_support: customers notified of mitigation progress. no SLA credits requested so far.
vikas_oncall: once fully stable (no 5xx change for 30m) we'll close INC-2026-103. postmortem assigned to me (vikas). will include root cause (upstream provider transit packet drop) and action items: DNS fallback automation, conntrack capacity autoscale, more aggressive health-check failover.
sarah_product: please include runbook tweaks and oncall checklist.
kevin_neteng: network action item: add BGP community to prefer alternate transit in AZ-D, and validate provider SLAs.
ashley: closing notes: incident severity downgraded to resolved at 11:45 UTC after stable metrics and no customer reports. will create postmortem draft.
vikas_oncall: thanks all. handoff to engineering for postmortem. final note: we saved ~95% of traffic by DNS shift + draining before provider fixed transit.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2026-103. Duration: 1h34m. Postmortem owner: vikas_oncall.
maria_support: posting final customer summary and closing tickets in 10m. :white_check_mark:
kevin_neteng: filing internal provider escalation ticket and CC'ing SRE leadership.
ashley: good work everyone.
